guide.title: Cannon Mountain, New Hampshire: state-owned skiing since 1929, tramway since 1938
guide.intro: New Hampshire State Parks describes Cannon Mountain as New Hampshire's only state-owned and operated ski area, located within Franconia Notch State Park and managed by the NH Division of Parks and Recreation, per the agency's own "About Us" page. Skiing on the mountain predates that arrangement: old logging roads were used for skiing starting in 1929, and the Richard Taft Race Course was developed in 1931-32, according to Wikipedia's "Cannon Mountain Ski Area" article.

sections.heading: The tramway, twice over
sections.body: New Hampshire State Parks describes its own tramway as "the first passenger aerial tramway in North America," which began operation on the site in 1938. The original tramway, Tram I, carried "almost seven million passengers" before being replaced in 1980 by Tram II, nicknamed "Ketchup and Mustard" for its red and yellow cable cars, per NH State Parks' own tramway page. Tram II ascended 2,180 feet vertically to a summit elevation of 4,080 feet, provided an 8-minute ride, and operated for 45 years before being closed and retired as of October 26, 2025, according to the same source. As of that page, a third-generation tram is in the design phase -- Cannon Mountain partnered with SCJ Alliance on structural analysis, expected to be complete in December 2025 -- and New Hampshire State Parks says that once built, Cannon will be the only mountain in North America to operate a third-generation aerial tram, though as of now no replacement tram is operating.

sections.heading: In Franconia
sections.body: New Hampshire State Parks' own Cannon Mountain Ski Area page states that "US Olympic skier Bode Miller grew up skiing at Cannon." The New England Ski Museum sits at the base of the tramway, within the town of Franconia, and describes itself as "a member supported non-profit organization dedicated to the history of skiing and the 10th Mountain Division," per its own website. Echo Lake, also within Franconia Notch State Park and the town of Franconia, is described by Cannon Mountain's own website as a "39-acre spring fed lake" with a sandy beach, open Thursday-Sunday, with pedal boat and kayak rentals available. The Frost Place, on Ridge Road, served as "Robert Frost's family home from 1915-1920" and is now described by its own website as "a permanent home and museum for poets and poetry," listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

faq.question: Is Cannon Mountain state-owned?
faq.answer: Yes. New Hampshire State Parks describes Cannon as New Hampshire's only state-owned and operated ski area, located within Franconia Notch State Park and managed by the NH Division of Parks and Recreation, per the agency's own "About Us" page.

faq.question: What happened to Cannon's aerial tramway?
faq.answer: New Hampshire State Parks describes the original 1938 tramway as "the first passenger aerial tramway in North America." It was replaced in 1980 by Tram II, which was closed and retired as of October 26, 2025; a third-generation replacement was in the design phase as of the state's own tramway page, with no replacement operating yet.
